The *Kakkaṭakarasadāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 54) is a canonical verse text in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The narrative describes a female deva who recounts the celestial splendor and happiness she attained as a karmic reward for having offered crab soup to the monastic community (Sangha) during her past human life [SuttaCentral]. Four translations of the text across four languages are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

No external cross-language parallels are cataloged on SuttaCentral or detected with significant scores in DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse, recording 202 matching segments shared across 33 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of its verses are quoted and explained in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (83 matches, with segments 1.1–8.4 corresponding to commentary paragraphs 2577_3–2603) and in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares extensive formulaic verse units with other stories in the *Vimānavatthu*, most prominently the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10), *Paṭhamanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 6), and *Sunikkhittavimānavatthu* (Vv 85) [DharmaNexus].
